title: Microproof playlet — seller snippets & fallback heuristics (draft)
summary: Compact, rep-facing 'microproof' deck and seller snippets for rapid pilots. Focus: 90s value pitch + fallback economics hooks + quick validation plan.
content:
Status: early draft / experiment notes

Purpose
- Create a tiny, repeatable set of seller assets (3 slides + 6 talking snippets) that SEs and AEs can use in pilot qualification and first demo.
- Emphasize microproofs: low-friction wins that prove latency/cost/reliability claims in 1–2 customer touchpoints.
- Include explicit fallback heuristics to handle objections about quality, scale, and cost.

Target audience- Platform/embedded engineers, platform/product owners, and SEs running initial POCs.
- Primary stage: pilot qualification -> proof-of-concept -> reserved capacity conversation.

Core claim (90s elevator)- "Redwood gives you predictable inference economics and uptime without building the serving stack. In a pilot we show measurable per-request cost savings via prefix caching and batching, plus a simple fallback path that keeps the feature live during traffic spikes."

Slide skeleton (3 slides, single-sheet speaker notes each)
1) What you get in a pilot (30s)
  - Headline: Predictable latency & cost for X requests/min
  - Bullet: we deploy a curated model variant, enable prefix cache, run with a 99th-p50 latency SLO and a cost baseline
  - Quick proof: show (mock) before/after token cost and p95 latency numbers (example numbers below)
  - NOTE to rep: call out customer-specific trigger (e.g., chat agent at checkout)

2) Fallback & reliability plan (30s)
  - Headline: graceful degradation keeps product live
  - Diagram text: primary model -> lightweight cache -> fallback variant (quantized or smaller model) -> degraded but acceptable output
  - Scripts: When latency > SLO for 3 consecutive min, automatically route 30% of traffic to fallback and escalate to on-call.
  - NOTE: show example of fallback that preserves intent for NLU tasks (use examples in appendix)

3) Validation & next steps (30s)
  - Headline: 2-week pilot checklist
  - Bullets: instrument metrics (cost/token, p50/p95, failed requests), run 3 prompt-scenarios for quality regression checks, handshake on success criteria for Reserved Capacity ask
  - CTA: request 1-week traffic sample + 2-week pilot commit

Seller snippets (6 quick lines to cover common flows)
- Qualification: "How important is consistent response time for this feature during peak loads?"
- Value hook: "We’ll show a per-request cost delta after we enable caching and batching — many teams see 20–40% reduction vs naive serving."
- Objection (quality): "If outputs degrade, we can fall back to a smaller verified model or return cached responses for identical prompts. That keeps the experience intact while we triage."
- Objection (security/compliance): "We can run Private deployment or Dedicated capacity with KMS integration for data retention requirements — minimal upfront infra from your side."
- Pilot ask: "Can we get a one-week sample of typical requests? We’ll return a pilot plan with expected p95 and cost projection within 48 hours."
- Closing: "If the pilot shows the expected economics and latency, we’ll propose a Reserved Capacity commitment tailored to peak concurrency."

Fallback heuristics (operational playbook excerpt)
- Trigger thresholds (example): p95 > 1.8s for > 5m window OR error rate > 1% -> move to fallback.
- Fallback split: initially 20–30% of traffic; if error persists after 10 minutes, escalate to 50% with concurrent alerting.
- Quality guardrail: run regression eval on 10 canonical prompts every hour when fallback active; if average acceptability < 70% rollback to primary and notify team.
- Communication script: "We’ve routed a subset of requests to a verified, smaller variant to keep the feature responsive; we’ll monitor quality and re-align in 30m."

Mock numbers to use in template (replace with real after pilot)
- Baseline (customer naive endpoint): p50 350ms, p95 1.9s, token cost $0.0018/token
- Redwood pilot w/ cache & batching: p50 220ms, p95 480ms, token cost $0.0011/token (est. 38% savings)
- Fallback variant (quantized): p50 120ms, p95 230ms, token cost $0.0005/token

Pilot validation plan (A/B checklist)
- Week 0: sample collection (1 week worth), define 6 canonical prompts and SLOs, sign pilot agreement
- Week 1: deploy pilot model variant + enable prefix caching and batching; collect metrics
- Week 2: run quality evaluation (automated prompts + small human sample), adjust routing policy, produce final pilot report
- Success criteria (any one): cost reduction >= 20% vs baseline OR p95 improvement >= 30% while maintain human-acceptable quality

Measurement dashboard (rep-facing fields to request)
- Traffic sample size, average tokens per request, peak RPS, top 10 user flows, SLA target, security constraints

Experiment variants to iterate on- V1: aggressive batching (larger batch windows) — better cost, higher p95 risk
- V2: aggressive prefix caching (cache TTL 60s) — best for repetitive prompts
- V3: fallback-ready flow (pre-warm quantized variant) — best reliability wins, slightly lower quality

A/B test plan (quick): run V1 for 3 days, measure cost and p95; switch to V2 for 3 days, compare; choose V3 only if reliability incidents occur.

Rep toolkit (what to send customers)
- 1-pager: pilot checklist + sample request list (1 slide)
- Micro-deck: 3 slides described above (PDF)
- 6-snippet cheat sheet (this doc)
- Playbook: fallback heuristics + contact list for SRE on-call

Notes to self / unresolved questions- Should we bake in a pre-written email template for sample requests? (YES)
- Do we want a canned demo that shows live fallback switching? (good idea, needs infra work)
- Need legal approval language for Private deployment notes (Ravi owns)
- Who will own the pilot report template? Maya to take first pass.
